inventory_limitations: The session serves operations only after Ghidra reports default auto-analysis complete; incomplete analysis does not expose partial results.

Ghidra Program checkpoint mode is disabled: closing discards metadata edits; original executable bytes are unchanged. For stock ELF/PE/Mach-O on Linux/macOS, set REA_GHIDRA_CHECKPOINT_DIR to a private absolute directory before starting REA (restart MCP after changing its startup environment).
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
External functions and local thunks are distinct; procedure metadata identifies both and preserves a thunk target when Ghidra resolves one.

Known provider defect ghidra-9996 (jump-table-flow-references-omitted): Ghidra 12.2 can omit jump-table flow references and emit incorrect decompiler output for clang -O0 x86-64 switches whose case labels start above zero. Upstream issue https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/issues/9996 is closed by c93917a622211349998f641de54cfdbe0e0e5bee, milestone 12.2.1, which is not yet released. This limitation is recorded for parsed 12.2 releases whose patch is below 12.2.1, including a zero patch and a suffix, and clears on 12.2.1. REA's verified switch lane compiles with -O2 and does not cover this shape.

Known provider defect ghidra-10154 (jump-table-unrecovered-function-truncated): Ghidra 12.2 leaves an aarch64 switch unrecovered when it is a byte-offset bounded by and-0xff. The function body stops at the indirect branch. Upstream issue https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/issues/10154 is open and names a Swift -O swift-enum switch; it has no fix commit and no milestone. REA reproduced the unrecovered jump table on the exact 12.2 build with an AArch64 ELF object of that instruction shape. A compare-bounded byte table still recovers. This record stays on every admitted build until a release is known to clear it.
